mainTopic: שינוי in גזילה: which changes make a stolen item the robber's, and when he pays the original value versus returning the item as it is
overview: The amud opens by finishing a question about a stolen לולב whose תיומת split. One version leaves the proof rejected. A second version brings רבי יהושע בן לוי, who says a split תיומת counts as removed, so the robber acquires the לולב. רב פפא then teaches that a change counts as שינוי only if the item cannot return to its original form: earth made into a brick or a bar made into coins can go back, but a brick crushed into earth or coins melted into a bar cannot, since rebuilding makes פנים חדשות. The משנה's 'זה הכלל' adds רבי אלעא's rule that a lamb that grew into a ram belongs to the thief. In the story of stolen oxen, רב נחמן makes a habitual robber pay half the land's improvement as a קנס, even though by strict law robbers pay according to the time of the robbery. A new משנה then separates two groups. When the item itself got worse (aged, cracked, rotted, soured), the thief pays the old value. When only its status changed, he returns it as it is. The גמרא explains that permanent weakening counts like aging. It then shows how רב can rule like רבי מאיר on slaves: in his version of the משנה, backed by ברייתות, the view that slaves are like land belongs to the majority.

steps.title: Trying to learn the split leaf from the removed leaf
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the rule for a removed תיומת should also apply to a split תיומת.
steps.simpleTranslation: What, isn't the same true when the middle leaf is split?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just had a source that a לולב whose תיומת was removed is פסול. Now it tries to stretch that ruling to a תיומת that only split.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a split תיומת is treated like a removed one, the לולב became פסול. That counts as a real change, so the robber would acquire it. The proof works only if 'removed' and 'split' are really the same.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What, isn't it...?' A formula for pushing a source toward a proof
the middle double leaf at the top of a לולב

phrases.english: What, is it not
that the same is true for where it became split?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the question about a split תיומת from before this section
steps.raayaObject: That a split תיומת makes the לולב פסול, so the robber acquires it
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling that a לולב whose תיומת was removed is פסול

steps.title: A removed leaf is different because something is missing
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off: a removed leaf leaves the לולב incomplete, but a split leaf is still all there.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. A removed leaf is different, because the לולב is missing something.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the תיומת is removed, the לולב is חסר, missing a part, so of course it is פסול. A split leaf is still attached, so the earlier ruling says nothing about it. In this version the proof fails; step 3 gives another version that settles the question.

phrases.english: No; where it was removed is different,
since it is lacking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof attempted in step 1
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the comparison between removed and split
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A removed leaf leaves the לולב incomplete; a split one does not

steps.title: Second version: a split leaf is like a removed one
steps.stepSummary: Another version brings רבי יהושע בן לוי, who says a split תיומת counts as removed and is פסול, and the גמרא learns from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: Come and hear. רבי מתון said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: if the middle leaf split, it is as if it were removed, and it is פסול. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of how the question ended. Here it is solved directly by a clear statement of רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי treats a split תיומת exactly like a removed one, so the לולב is פסול. That makes the split a real change, and the robber acquires the לולב. 'שמע מינה' closes the question in this version.

keyTerms.meaning: come and hear: introduces a source as proof
learn from this: the proof is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: In this second version, a split תיומת counts as removed, so the לולב is פסול and the robber acquires it.
steps.confusionAlert: Steps 1-2 and step 3 are two different versions of the same discussion, not one argument that continues. In the first version the question stays open; in the second it is solved.

phrases.english: There are those who say: Come and hear,
for Rabbi Matun said
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
If the middle leaf became split,
it becomes as if it were removed, and it is unfit!
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different version that solves what steps 1-2 left open
steps.raayaObject: A split תיומת makes the לולב פסול, which counts as a change
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי מתון in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In this version, the robber acquires a לולב whose תיומת split

steps.title: Earth made into a brick is not acquired
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that a robber who turns stolen earth into a brick does not acquire it, because the brick can be turned back into earth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Someone who stole earth and made it into a brick does not acquire it. Why? Because he can turn it back into earth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: רב פפא's rule about which changes let a robber keep stolen material.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שינוי only gives the robber ownership if it is a real, lasting change. A brick can easily be crushed back into earth, so the earth never truly changed. The robber must return it.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a test for שינוי קונה: a change that can be undone, returning the item to its original form, is not a real change.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
This one who robbed earth from his fellow,
and made it into a brick, does not acquire it.
What is the reason?
Because he can go back and make it earth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הַאי מַאן דִּגְזַל עַפְרָא מֵחַבְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic within the laws of שינוי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Earth made into a brick is not acquired, since it can go back to being earth

steps.title: A brick made into earth is acquired
steps.stepSummary: The reverse case: a stolen brick crushed into earth does become the robber's.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he stole a brick and made it into earth, he acquires it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the opposite case to contrast with step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Crushing a brick destroys its form for good. The original brick can never come back, so this is a real שינוי, and the robber acquires it and pays its value.

phrases.english: A brick, and he made it into earth: he acquires it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The contrasting case to step 4
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A brick turned into earth is acquired by the robber

steps.title: But he could rebuild the brick
steps.stepSummary: An objection to step 5: the earth could be made back into a brick, just as in step 4.
steps.simpleTranslation: What might you say? Maybe he can go back and make it into a brick?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible challenge to the rule in step 5. It sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said a change that can be reversed is not a real change. So the challenge asks: the earth can also be turned back into a brick, so why isn't this change reversible too?

keyTerms.meaning: what would you say? It introduces a possible objection

phrases.english: What would you say?
Perhaps he will go back and make it a brick?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אָמְרַתְּ – דִּלְמָא הָדַר וְעָבֵיד לֵיהּ לְבֵינְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 5 using the reasoning of step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a brick turned into earth is acquired
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If reversibility cancels a שינוי, the earth can be made back into a brick, so the change should not count

steps.title: A rebuilt brick is a brand-new brick
steps.stepSummary: Answer: a brick made from the earth is a different brick, a new entity, not the original one returning.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is a different brick, and a new thing has come here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earth made back into a brick does not bring back the original brick. It creates a new brick (פנים חדשות). So the original item cannot really return. In step 4, by contrast, the original earth really comes back as earth.
steps.whatToRemember: A change counts as שינוי when the original form cannot truly return. Rebuilding the shape makes a new item (פנים חדשות), not the old one.

phrases.english: This is a different brick,
and a new entity has come here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the rebuilt item is a new entity
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Making the earth into a brick again would undo the change
steps.terutzMaskana: The new brick is פנים חדשות, so the original never returns and the שינוי stands

steps.title: A silver bar made into coins is not acquired
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא's parallel rule: a stolen silver bar made into coins is not acquired, because the coins can be melted back into a bar.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא also said: Someone who stole a silver bar and made it into coins does not acquire it. Why? He can turn them back into a bar.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a second case that follows the same pattern as the earth and brick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Melting coins brings the silver back to a plain bar, its original form. Since the change can be undone, it is not a real שינוי, and the robber must return it.

keyTerms.meaning: a bar or ingot of silver

phrases.english: And Rav Pappa said:
This one who robbed a silver bar from his fellow,
and made it into coins, does not acquire it.
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets, 'and made it', is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
He can go back and make them a silver bar.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הַאי מַאן דִּגְזַל נְסָכָא מֵחַבְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ruling to step 4
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A silver bar made into coins is not acquired, since the coins can be melted back

steps.title: Coins made into a silver bar are acquired
steps.stepSummary: The reverse: stolen coins melted into a bar become the robber's.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he stole coins and made them into a silver bar, he acquires them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the contrasting case, matching the brick-into-earth case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Melting destroys the coins, and the original coins can never come back. So this is a real שינוי, and the robber acquires them.

phrases.english: Coins, and he made them into a silver bar: he acquires them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The contrasting case to step 8
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Coins melted into a bar are acquired by the robber

steps.title: But he could mint coins again
steps.stepSummary: The same objection as before: the bar can be made back into coins.
steps.simpleTranslation: What might you say? That he can go back and make them coins?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the challenge from the brick case, now about coins. It sets up the answer that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a reversible change is not a שינוי, the bar can be minted back into coins. So why does melting the coins count?

phrases.english: What would you say?
That he can go back and make them coins?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אָמְרַתְּ – הָדַר עָבֵיד לְהוּ זוּזֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 9 using the reasoning of step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that coins melted into a bar are acquired
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The bar can be made back into coins, so the change seems reversible

steps.title: New coins are a new entity
steps.stepSummary: Answer: coins minted again are new coins, not the original ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: A new thing has come here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with the same idea it used for the brick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Re-minted coins are פנים חדשות, brand-new coins. The original coins are gone forever, so melting them was a real שינוי and the robber acquires them.
steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא's rule: if the change can bring back the very same original form, it is not a שינוי. If the original form is gone and any rebuilding makes something new (פנים חדשות), it is a שינוי and the robber acquires the item.

phrases.english: A new entity has come here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 using the same reasoning as step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the rebuilt item is a new entity
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Minting coins again would undo the change
steps.terutzMaskana: New coins are פנים חדשות, so the שינוי stands and the robber acquires them

steps.title: Cleaning old coins versus blackening new coins
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא adds a rule about coins: making blackened coins look new is not a real change, but making new coins black is a real change that makes them the robber's.
steps.simpleTranslation: If stolen coins were old and blackened and he made them shiny like new, he does not acquire them. If they were new and he made them black, he does acquire them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא continues his list of rules about stolen coins, now about the coins' appearance: old and dark versus new and shiny.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same test as before. Cleaned old coins can turn black again, so the change can be undone and they still belong to the owner. Turning new coins black counts as a change, so the robber acquires them and only owes money; the next steps explain why blackening cannot really be undone.

keyTerms.meaning: He acquires (the stolen item becomes his)

phrases.english: If they were blackened and he made them new
phrases.notes: This is still רב פפא talking about stolen coins from the earlier steps.

phrases.english: he does not acquire them.
If they were new and he made them blackened
he acquires them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב פפא's series of coin rules after the silver bar and coins cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Making blackened coins new is not a change of ownership; blackening new coins is a change, and the robber acquires them.

steps.title: But he can clean the blackened coins again
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises the familiar objection: if the robber blackened new coins, he could just clean them and make them new again, so maybe the change can be undone.
steps.simpleTranslation: What would you say: that he can go back and make them new again?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises the same kind of objection it used before: the change seems reversible, because the blackened coins could be cleaned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier steps, a change that can be undone did not count as a real change. Here it looks like blackening can be undone by cleaning, so why does the robber acquire the coins?

keyTerms.meaning: What would you say? (introduces a possible objection)

phrases.english: What would you say:
that he can go back and make them new?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אָמְרַתְּ – הָדַר עָבֵיד לְהוּ חַדְתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second half of step 12 using the reversibility test from steps 10-11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that blackening new coins makes them the robber's.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A change that can be reversed is not a real change, and blackened coins can be cleaned back to new.

steps.title: The blackening still shows
steps.stepSummary: Answer: even after cleaning, you can tell the coins were once blackened, so they never truly return to their original new state.
steps.simpleTranslation: Their blackening is clearly known.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that cleaning cannot fully undo the blackening, because the marks of age stay visible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once new coins are blackened, they can never look truly new again. So the change cannot really be undone, and it counts as a real change.

keyTerms.meaning: It is clearly known, it can be recognized

steps.whatToRemember: A change only counts if the item cannot truly go back to how it was. Cleaning old coins does not count, but blackening new coins does, because the blackening always shows.

phrases.english: Their blackening is clearly known.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual clarification: the change is not truly reversible.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Cleaning blackened coins returns them to their original state.
steps.terutzMaskana: The blackening stays recognizable, so the coins never truly return to new, and the change counts.

steps.title: What does 'this is the principle' add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's general rule that all robbers pay according to the time of the robbery, and asks what the words 'זה הכלל' come to include.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: This is the principle: all robbers pay according to the time of the robbery. What does 'this is the principle' come to add?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה and asks what extra case is hinted at by the words 'זה הכלל'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes that when a משנה says 'זה הכלל', it is including a case not already spelled out. So it asks which new case is meant.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the principle (often hints at an extra case)
According to the time of the robbery
What does it come to include?

phrases.english: This is the principle:
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה.

phrases.english: All robbers pay according to the time of the robbery.
'This is the principle' comes to include what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which additional case is included by the words 'זה הכלל'.

steps.title: A stolen lamb that grows into a ram
steps.stepSummary: The words come to include רבי אלעא's ruling: if a stolen lamb became a ram, or a calf became an ox, the growth is a change and the thief acquires it; if he then slaughters or sells it, it is his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: It includes what רבי אלעא said: if someone stole a lamb and it became a ram, or a calf and it became an ox, a change happened while it was with him and he acquired it. If he slaughtered or sold it, he slaughters his own and sells his own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'זה הכלל' includes רבי אלעא's case of an animal that grew up while stolen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Growing from a young animal into an adult counts as a שינוי, so the thief acquires it and only pays its value from the time of the theft. Since it is now his, slaughtering or selling it is done to his own animal.

keyTerms.meaning: A change in the stolen item

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a natural change, like an animal growing up, also counts as a שינוי that transfers ownership to the thief.

phrases.english: To include that which Rabbi Ela said:
If one stole a lamb and it became a ram,
a calf and it became an ox,
a change occurred in his possession, and he acquired it.
If he slaughtered or sold it,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלּוֹ הוּא טוֹבֵחַ, שֶׁלּוֹ הוּא מוֹכֵר.
phrases.english: he slaughters his own, he sells his own.
phrases.notes: So he does not owe the extra four- or five-times fine for slaughtering or selling a stolen animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'זה הכלל' includes רבי אלעא's ruling that an animal's growth while stolen is a change that makes it the thief's.

steps.title: The stolen oxen used for plowing
steps.stepSummary: A man stole a pair of oxen, plowed and sowed with them, then returned them. רב נחמן ruled that the improvement to the land should be assessed.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man robbed his friend of a pair of oxen. He went and plowed with them and sowed seeds with them, and in the end returned them to their owner. The case came before רב נחמן, who told them: Go assess the improvement that was gained.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about stolen oxen used for farm work and gives רב נחמן's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oxen came back unchanged, but the robber's land gained value from their work. רב נחמן says to assess that gain, meaning the robber must pay for it.

phrases.english: A certain man who robbed
a pair of oxen from his fellow,
went and plowed with them,
and sowed seeds with them.
In the end he returned them to their owner.
He came before Rav Naḥman.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: זִילוּ שׁוּמוּ שְׁבָחָא דְּאַשְׁבַּח.
phrases.english: He said to them: Go assess the improvement that was gained.
phrases.notes: He means the extra value the robber's land gained from the oxen's work.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דִּגְזַל פַּדָּנָא דְּתוֹרֵי מֵחַבְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a practical case connected to the rule that robbers pay according to the time of the robbery.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן: assess the improvement the robber gained from using the stolen oxen.

steps.title: Did only the oxen improve the land?
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב נחמן: the land also improved by itself, so why credit all the gain to the oxen?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Did only the oxen improve it? Did the land not improve on its own?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא objects to רב נחמן's ruling about assessing the improvement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not all the gain came from the oxen's work; the land itself also produces growth. So making the robber pay for the whole gain seems unfair.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
Did the oxen improve it, and the land did not improve it?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: תּוֹרֵי אַשְׁבֻּח, אַרְעָא לָא אַשְׁבַּח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's ruling in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling to assess the improvement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The land contributed to the gain too, so the oxen should not get credit for all of it.

steps.title: Only half the improvement
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that he never meant all of the improvement, only half.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Did I say they should assess all of it? I said half!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן clarifies his ruling to answer רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן agrees that the land also helped. So the owner of the oxen gets only half of the improvement, not the whole thing.

phrases.english: He said: Did I say they should assess all of it?
I said half!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying the scope of the original ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן meant the robber pays the full improvement.
steps.terutzMaskana: He meant only half, since the land also contributed.

steps.title: A robber only returns what he took
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges again: the oxen were stolen and came back in the same condition, and the משנה says robbers pay according to the time of the robbery, so why pay anything extra?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: In the end, it is a stolen item, and it is returned as it was, as we learned: All robbers pay according to the time of the robbery!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back a second time, now using the משנה's general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A robber's duty is to return the stolen item as it was when he took it. The oxen came back in that condition, so by the משנה's rule he seemingly owes nothing for the improvement, not even half.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not arguing about how much the land helped anymore. He is now saying the robber may owe nothing for the improvement at all, since he returned the oxen as they were.

phrases.english: He said to him: In the end,
it is a stolen item, and it is returned as it was,

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: כׇּל הַגַּזְלָנִין מְשַׁלְּמִין כִּשְׁעַת הַגְּזֵלָה!
phrases.english: as we learned: All robbers pay according to the time of the robbery!
phrases.notes: This is the same line from the משנה quoted in step 15.

steps.triggerLanguage: סוֹף סוֹף, גְּזֵילָה הוּא – וְקָא הָדְרָה בְּעֵינַאּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Renews the attack on רב נחמן's ruling even after the 'half' clarification in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that the robber pays half the improvement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A robber only has to return the stolen item as it was at the time of the robbery; the oxen came back unchanged, so no payment for improvement should be owed.

steps.title: רב נחמן: My ruling was a fine on a known robber
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן tells רבא not to question him while he sits in judgment, since he is an expert in monetary law. He explains that he made this thief pay extra as a penalty, because the man is a known, long-time robber.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Didn't I tell you not to say anything to me while I am judging? Our friend הונא said about me, 'שבור מלכא and I are equals in monetary law.' This man is an old, experienced robber, and I want to fine him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רבא's challenge from Step 20. He admits that by the strict rule the thief would not have to pay extra. He made him pay anyway as a special fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא had asked why the thief pays anything extra, since the oxen came back in the same condition. רב נחמן does not argue with the rule. He explains that this ruling was a קנס, a penalty for this particular habitual robber. His expertise in monetary law, which הונא praised, is his reason for asking רבא not to interrupt him while he judges.

keyTerms.meaning: A fine or penalty; 'I will fine him'
An 'old robber'; someone who has been stealing for a long time

steps.whatToRemember: The ruling to assess half the land's improvement was not the basic law. It was a special fine on a habitual robber. By the strict rule, a robber pays according to the time of the robbery.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't conclude that every thief who works with stolen animals must pay for the improvement they produced. רב נחמן himself says this was a special penalty for this one man.

phrases.english: He said to him: Didn't I tell you,
when I sit in judgment
don't say anything to me,
since Huna, our friend, said about me:
"I and King Shapur are brothers in monetary law"?
phrases.notes: "King Shapur" is a nickname for שמואל. Huna means רב נחמן's rulings in money matters are as weighty as שמואל's.

phrases.english: This man is an old, experienced robber,
and I want to fine him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's second challenge (Step 20) by calling the payment a penalty rather than the basic law.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recasting the ruling as a קנס (penalty), not the strict rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא thought רב נחמן was stating the basic law, which would contradict the rule that robbers pay according to the time of the robbery.
steps.terutzMaskana: The basic rule stands. רב נחמן made this habitual robber pay extra only as a fine.

steps.title: משנה: A stolen animal or slaves that grew old
steps.stepSummary: If a thief stole an animal or slaves and they grew old with him, he pays their value at the time of the robbery. רבי מאיר says that with slaves he may simply return them as they are.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone stole an animal and it grew old, or slaves and they grew old, he pays according to their value at the time of the robbery. רבי מאיר says: with slaves, he says to the owner, 'Here is yours in front of you.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It discusses stolen items that lost value while with the thief, starting with an animal and slaves that aged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Aging counts as a change, so the thief cannot just hand back the weaker animal or slave. He must pay the higher value from when he stole it. רבי מאיר treats slaves differently: the thief may return them as they are now, even though they are worth less.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of a new משנה
He pays the value from the time of the robbery
'Here is yours before you'; the thief returns the item as it is now

phrases.english: Mishnah:
If he stole an animal and it grew old,
or slaves and they grew old,
he pays according to the time of the robbery.
Rabbi Meir says: with slaves,
he says to him: "Here is yours before you."
phrases.notes: The thief hands back the slaves as they are now, without paying for the value they lost.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of the stolen oxen ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A thief whose stolen animal or slaves aged pays their value at the time of the robbery. רבי מאיר says that with slaves he may return them as they are.

steps.title: משנה: A cracked coin, rotted fruit, soured wine
steps.stepSummary: If the stolen coin cracked, the fruit rotted, or the wine turned sour, the thief pays according to the value at the time of the robbery.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he stole a coin and it cracked, fruit and it rotted, or wine and it turned sour, he pays according to the time of the robbery.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with more examples of stolen items that got damaged while with the thief.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These cases follow the same rule as the aging animal. The item itself got physically worse, so the thief cannot just return it. He pays what it was worth when he stole it.

phrases.english: If he stole a coin and it cracked;
fruit and it rotted;
wine and it turned sour;
he pays according to the time of the robbery.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more cases that follow the 'pay according to the time of the robbery' rule from Step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a stolen coin cracked, fruit rotted, or wine soured, the thief pays the value at the time of the robbery.

steps.title: משנה: Cases where the thief returns the item as it is
steps.stepSummary: In several cases the thief may simply hand back the item, even though it is now worth little or nothing: a coin taken out of use, תרומה that became impure, חמץ after פסח, and an animal that became unfit for the מזבח or was sentenced to stoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the coin was taken out of use, the תרומה became impure, the חמץ had פסח pass over it, or a sin was done with the animal, or it became unfit for the מזבח, or it was being taken out to be stoned, he says to the owner, 'Here is yours in front of you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now lists the opposite group: cases where the thief does not pay the old value. He just returns the item in its current state.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In these cases the object itself did not crack, rot, or age. What changed is its use or status: a government decision, impurity, a prohibition, or unfitness for an offering. So the thief can say 'here is yours,' even though the item may now be worth very little or nothing at all.

keyTerms.meaning: It was invalidated; the coin was taken out of use
חמץ that was owned during פסח; forbidden to benefit from afterward
It became unfit to be offered on the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has two groups. When the item itself got physically worse (it aged, cracked, rotted, or soured), the thief pays the value from the time of the robbery. When only its status or usability changed (a coin taken out of use, impurity, חמץ after פסח, unfit for the מזבח, sentenced to stoning), the thief may return it as is.
steps.confusionAlert: A coin shows up in both groups. If it cracked, he pays its old value. If it was taken out of use by the government, he just returns it. The difference is whether the coin itself was damaged.

phrases.english: A coin and it was invalidated;
תרומה and it became impure;
leavened bread and Passover passed over it;
an animal with which a sin was done,
or that became unfit for the altar,
or that was going out to be stoned,
he says to him: "Here is yours before you."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with Step 23 by listing cases where the thief returns the item as it is instead of paying its original value.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a stolen item lost value only through a change in status or usability, the thief returns it as it is: 'Here is yours before you.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This contrast between damage to the item itself and a change in its status sets up the גמרא's coming discussion of these cases.

steps.title: רב פפא: Weakening Also Counts Like Aging
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the משנה's word 'aged' also includes an animal that became weak.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב פפא says: 'Aged' does not have to mean truly old. Even if the animal only became weak, the thief pays what it was worth at the time of the robbery.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion of the משנה. רב פפא widens the case of an animal that 'aged' so it also covers an animal that became weak.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that if a stolen animal grew old, the thief pays its value from the time of the robbery. רב פפא adds that a smaller change, weakening, works the same way. The change counts, so the thief owns the animal and just pays the old value.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Pappa says:
'Aged' does not mean it actually aged,
phrases.notes: He is quoting the משנה's word about a stolen animal that grew old while the thief had it.

phrases.english: but even if it grew weak.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לֹא ״הִזְקִינָה״ – הִזְקִינָה מַמָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא on the משנה case of an animal that aged (Step 22).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A stolen animal that became weak counts as changed, just like one that aged.

steps.title: But the משנה Said Aged
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the משנה says 'aged,' so how can weakening be enough?
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה 'aged'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפא using the exact word of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Old age is a big change that never goes away. Since the משנה picked that word, it seems to say that a smaller change like weakening does not count.

phrases.english: But we learned 'aged'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב פפא's wider reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that weakening counts like aging.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה chose the word 'aged,' which suggests that only a lasting, major change counts.

steps.title: Weakness That Never Goes Away
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא meant a weakness so severe that the animal will never recover, which is just like old age.
steps.simpleTranslation: He meant weakness like old age, where the animal will not become healthy again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב פפא was only talking about permanent weakness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key point is that the change is permanent. Old age never goes away, and neither does this kind of weakness, so both count as a real change. A weakness the animal can recover from would not count.

phrases.english: Weakened in a way like aging,
so that it will not become healthy again.
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is the corrected spelling, which some versions add.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by narrowing רב פפא's statement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב פפא seemed to mean any weakening at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only permanent weakness, which is like old age, counts as a change.
steps.whatToRemember: A change only counts if it is lasting. Permanent weakness is treated like old age.

steps.title: A Lamb That Grew Into a Ram Belongs to the Thief
steps.stepSummary: מר קשישא tells רב אשי a teaching said in the name of רבי יוחנן: growing up is a change, so the thief owns the animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר קשישא son of רב חסדא said to רב אשי: This is what they say in the name of רבי יוחנן: Even if he stole a lamb and it became a ram, or a calf and it became an ox, a change happened while it was with him, and he owns it. If he slaughtered or sold it, he is slaughtering and selling his own animal.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement is brought: even natural growing up counts as a change that makes the stolen animal the thief's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the change was the animal getting worse. Here the animal grew up, and that also counts. Since it is now the thief's own animal, slaughtering or selling it does not make him pay the extra fine for slaughtering or selling a stolen animal.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר קַשִּׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא
phrases.english: Mar Kashisha son of Rav Chisda said
to Rav Ashi: This is what they say
in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
Even if he stole a lamb and it became a ram,
or a calf and it became an ox,
a change happened in his hands, and he acquired it.
If he slaughtered or sold it,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלּוֹ הוּא טוֹבֵחַ, שֶׁלּוֹ הוּא מוֹכֵר.
phrases.english: he slaughters his own, he sells his own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another kind of change to the discussion: growing up instead of getting worse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Natural growth, like a lamb becoming a ram, is a change that gives the thief ownership, so he is exempt from the four-or-five fine.

steps.title: רב אשי Corrects Who Said It
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי tells מר קשישא not to mix up names. That teaching was said in the name of רבי אלעא, not רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Didn't I tell you not to switch the people? That statement was said in the name of רבי אלעא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי does not argue with the rule. He only corrects who said it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The law itself stays the same. What is rejected is the name it was quoted in: it belongs to רבי אלעא. The גמרא cares about quoting each teaching in the name of the person who really said it.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't switch the people (whose names you quote)

phrases.english: He said to him: Didn't I tell you:
Do not switch the men?
That was said in the name of Rabbi Ela.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו אָמֵינָא לָךְ: לָא תַּחְלֵיף גַּבְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Corrects the name given in Step 28.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the name it was quoted in, not the law.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The teaching was wrongly quoted in the name of רבי יוחנן. It was really said in the name of רבי אלעא.

steps.title: רב Rules Like רבי מאיר on Slaves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי מאיר's view in the משנה, and רב rules that the הלכה follows him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: With slaves, the thief tells the owner, 'Here is yours in front of you.' רב חנינא בר אבדימי says that רב says: The הלכה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, רבי מאיר's view about slaves, and brings רב's ruling that the הלכה follows him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that a slave who grew old can simply be handed back as he is. רב rules this way. This sets up the next question, since רבי מאיר seems to be a lone voice against the majority.

keyTerms.meaning: Here is yours in front of you

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
With slaves, he says to him: 'Here is yours in front of you.'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חֲנִינָא בַּר אַבְדִּימִי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Chanina bar Avdimi says that Rav says:
The halacha follows Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חֲנִינָא בַּר אַבְדִּימִי אָמַר רַב: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה (Step 22) and takes up רבי מאיר's view about slaves.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב rules that a stolen slave who aged may be returned as he is.

steps.title: Would רב Leave the Majority
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: would רב really ignore the majority of חכמים and follow רבי מאיר alone?
steps.simpleTranslation: And would רב leave the רבנן and act like רבי מאיר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's ruling, because the normal rule is to follow the majority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the רבנן (the majority) say the thief pays the value from the time of the robbery, and only רבי מאיר says slaves can be returned as they are. Ruling like a single opinion against the majority needs an explanation.

phrases.english: And would Rav leave the Rabbis
and act like Rabbi Meir?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב שָׁבֵיק רַבָּנַן וְעָבֵיד כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's ruling.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The halacha normally follows the majority (רבנן) over one person.

steps.title: A ברייתא Has the Opinions Reversed
steps.stepSummary: The answer: a ברייתא teaches the opinions the other way around, so the 'return as is' view belongs to the majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: Because a ברייתא teaches it the opposite way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that in a ברייתא, the 'return the slave as he is' view is said by the רבנן, the majority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא is right, רב is not leaving the majority at all. He is following the majority as the ברייתא records it.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

phrases.english: They say: Because a ברייתא teaches it the opposite way.
phrases.notes: In the ברייתא, the רבנן are the ones who say a slave can be handed back as he is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different source with the names reversed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב was following a lone opinion.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to the ברייתא, רב is following the majority.

steps.title: Would רב Leave the משנה for a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: would רב follow a ברייתא over our משנה?
steps.simpleTranslation: And would רב leave the משנה and act like the ברייתא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: the משנה is the main source, so why rely on the ברייתא?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is usually trusted more than a ברייתא. So relying on the ברייתא's version to go against the משנה still seems strange.

phrases.english: And would Rav leave the משנה
and act like the ברייתא?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 32.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that relies on the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה is normally preferred over a ברייתא.

steps.title: רב Reads the משנה Reversed Too
steps.stepSummary: The answer: רב also reads the משנה with the opinions reversed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב reads the משנה the opposite way too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that in רב's reading, the משנה matches the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the משנה and the ברייתא agree, so רב is not going against the משנה. But the wording here sounds like רב himself chose to switch the משנה, and that sets up the next question.

phrases.english: Rav reads the משנה the opposite way too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 33.
steps.terutzMaskana: In רב's reading the משנה agrees with the ברייתא.

steps.title: Why Not Fix the ברייתא Instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: why change the משנה to match the ברייתא? It would make more sense to change the ברייתא to match the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is רב's reason for reversing the משנה because of the ברייתא? On the contrary, let him reverse the ברייתא because of the משנה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that רב switched the משנה on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If two sources disagree, the weaker one (the ברייתא) should be adjusted to fit the stronger one (the משנה), not the other way around.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of, in the face of

phrases.english: And what is Rav's reason
that he reverses the משנה because of the ברייתא?
On the contrary, let him reverse the ברייתא because of the משנה!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי טַעְמֵיהּ דְּרַב דְּאָפֵיךְ מַתְנִיתִין מִקַּמֵּי דְּבָרַיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in Step 34.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רב reversed the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The weaker source (the ברייתא) should be adjusted to fit the stronger one (the משנה), not the other way.

steps.title: רב Was Taught the משנה That Way
steps.stepSummary: The final answer: רב did not change anything. He was taught the משנה with the opinions reversed.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: רב was also taught the משנה the opposite way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רב's version of the משנה already had the opinions reversed. He did not switch it himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב received a different version of the משנה, and it matches the ברייתא. So רב is following both a משנה and the majority. No source was changed to fit another.
steps.confusionAlert: 'הלכה כרבי מאיר' refers to the view our משנה gives to רבי מאיר: a slave can be returned as he is. In רב's own version, that same view belongs to the רבנן, the majority.
steps.whatToRemember: רב rules that a stolen slave who aged can be returned as he is. He is not going against the majority, because his version of the משנה, like the ברייתא, gives this view to the רבנן.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי: רַב נָמֵי מַתְנִיתִין אִיפְּכָא אַתְנוּיָהּ.
phrases.english: They say: Rav was also taught the משנה the opposite way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 35. Step 37 then offers a second answer, and steps 41-42 go on to discuss the wording of רב's ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying the source: a different version that was handed down
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב himself chose to switch the משנה to fit the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב was taught the משנה with the opinions reversed, so it already matched the ברייתא.

steps.title: רב reverses a משנה when two ברייתות disagree with it
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: רב would not reverse a משנה because of one ברייתא, but he would reverse it because of two.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say this instead: רב does not reverse a משנה when there is only one ברייתא against it. When there are two ברייתות against it, he does reverse it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer to the question of how רב could change the משנה. He really did reverse it, because two ברייתות go against it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 36 the answer was that רב was simply taught the משנה reversed. Here the גמרא says something different: רב did choose to reverse it. That is allowed because one ברייתא is not enough to override a משנה, but two ברייתות together are. This means the גמרא now has to show us a second ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you prefer, say this instead (it brings a second answer)
He reverses (switches the names of who holds what)

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
When he does not reverse,
that is one [משנה] in light of one [ברייתא];
one in light of two, he does reverse.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: כִּי לָא אָפֵיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the question in step 35, in place of the answer in step 36.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rule about when a משנה may be reversed: two ברייתות outweigh one משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רב would never change a משנה because of a ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: He would not change it because of one ברייתא, but he would because of two.

steps.title: The second ברייתא: who owns the newborn after a trade or sale
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting the second ברייתא. In a dispute over when an animal or maidservant gave birth, a sure claim against silence wins, and if both say 'I don't know', they split.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: Someone traded a cow for a donkey and the cow gave birth. Or someone sold his maidservant and she gave birth. If one says 'she gave birth while she was mine' and the other is silent, the first one gets the baby. If both say 'I don't know', they split it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the second ברייתא it promised. These first cases set up the background before we reach the part that matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is about whether the birth happened before or after the trade. That decides who owns the baby. Someone who makes a sure claim against someone who stays silent wins, and when both are unsure, they divide. These cases prepare for the main case, where both sides make a sure claim.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
One who trades (swaps one item for another)
While it was in my possession (while I owned it)

phrases.english: As it is taught:
One who exchanges a cow for a donkey, and it gave birth;
and similarly, one who sells his maidservant, and she gave birth;
this one says: 'She gave birth in my possession,'
and the other is silent: he acquires it.
This one says: 'I do not know,'
and that one says: 'I do not know': they divide.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the second ברייתא that step 37 relied on.
steps.raayaObject: That a second ברייתא agrees with the reversed reading.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about a traded cow or sold maidservant who gave birth.

steps.title: When both claim the birth: רבי מאיר says the seller swears
steps.stepSummary: If both sides say 'she gave birth while she was mine', רבי מאיר says the seller swears and keeps the baby, because a person who swears a Torah oath swears and does not pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: If each one says 'she gave birth while she was mine', the seller swears that she gave birth while she was his. This is because everyone who swears a Torah oath swears and then does not pay. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the case where both sides make a sure claim. רבי מאיר says the seller swears and wins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seller is the one who had the mother at first, so he is the one being claimed from. His oath frees him from giving up the baby. This ruling applies to the sold maidservant too, so רבי מאיר allows an oath about slaves. That means he does not treat slaves like land.

keyTerms.meaning: They swear and do not pay

phrases.english: This one says: 'In my possession,'
and that one says: 'In my possession':
the seller shall swear that she gave birth in his possession,
because all who take oaths that are in the Torah
swear and do not pay;
these are the words of רבי מאיר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the case where both sides make a sure claim.
steps.raayaObject: רבי מאיר allows an oath even about a maidservant, so he does not treat slaves like land.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling of רבי מאיר in the ברייתא.

steps.title: The חכמים: no oath on slaves or land
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say there is no oath about slaves or about land. This shows they treat slaves like land, which supports רב's reversed reading of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: we do not swear about slaves, and we do not swear about land.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of the ברייתא and the actual proof. The חכמים put slaves in the same group as land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the חכמים treat slaves like land, they are the ones who would also say about a stolen slave 'here is yours in front of you', just as with land. So in this ברייתא as well, the 'return as is' view belongs to the חכמים and not to רבי מאיר. That makes two ברייתות against the משנה, which is enough for רב to reverse it.
steps.whatToRemember: רב reverses the משנה because two ברייתות both show that it is the חכמים, not רבי מאיר, who treat slaves like land and say 'here is yours in front of you'.
steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא never actually talks about stolen slaves. The proof comes only from the fact that the חכמים put slaves in the same group as land.
steps.whyThisMatters: It completes the second answer by showing a second source against the משנה, so רב's ruling stands on solid ground.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
one does not take an oath, neither concerning slaves
nor concerning land.
phrases.notes: By grouping slaves with land, the חכמים show they treat slaves like land. That is the whole point of bringing this ברייתא.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵין נִשְׁבָּעִין לֹא עַל הָעֲבָדִים וְלֹא עַל הַקַּרְקָעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא with the opinion of the חכמים, which is the actual proof.
steps.raayaObject: The חכמים treat slaves like land, so the 'return as is' view belongs to them.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The statement of the חכמים in the ברייתא: there is no oath on slaves or on land.

steps.title: רב's wording does not fit his own version
steps.stepSummary: If רב learned the משנה reversed, his ruling should have been worded 'the הלכה follows the חכמים,' not 'the הלכה follows רבי מאיר.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this really 'the הלכה follows רבי מאיר'?! He should have said 'the הלכה follows the חכמים'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of רב's ruling. It says the wording does not match the reversed version of the משנה that רב himself used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that in רב's version, the view 'here is yours before you' belongs to the חכמים, not to רבי מאיר. So when רב agrees with that view, he should name the חכמים. Calling it רבי מאיר's view seems to contradict his own reading.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law: whose opinion we follow
The חכמים, the majority of the sages in the משנה
He should have said; it was needed for him to say

phrases.english: This: 'the halakha is like Rabbi Meir'?!
phrases.notes: This is רב's ruling quoted earlier on the daf, about stolen slaves who grew old.

phrases.english: He should have said: 'the halakha is like the Rabbis'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After proving that רב learned the משנה reversed, the גמרא now finds a problem in the wording of רב's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of רב's ruling, 'הלכה כרבי מאיר'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In רב's reversed version, the opinion he follows belongs to the חכמים, so naming רבי מאיר seems wrong.

steps.title: רב was speaking in terms of his listeners' version
steps.stepSummary: רב meant: according to the way you learn the משנה, which is the reverse of my version, the הלכה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: according to the way you reversed it and taught it, the הלכה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the wording problem. רב was talking to people who learned the משנה the other way, so he used the name found in their version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב's own version, the view 'here is yours before you' belongs to the חכמים. His listeners learned the משנה the other way and called this view רבי מאיר's. So 'הלכה כרבי מאיר' means 'follow the view that you call רבי מאיר's.' רב's ruling about what the law is stays exactly the same; only the name changes.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means; introduces a re-explanation of a statement
That you reversed (switched the names of who said what)
You taught; you learn the משנה this way

steps.whatToRemember: רב follows the view 'here is yours before you' for slaves, because slaves are like land. He called it רבי מאיר's view only because that is the name it has in his listeners' version of the משנה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב switched sides here. He still holds the same law. The answer only explains which name he used for that view.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying: according to what you reversed and taught,
phrases.notes: 'You reversed' is said from רב's side: his listeners learn the משנה the opposite way from him.

phrases.english: the halakha is like Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of step 41.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the statement: the name 'רבי מאיר' refers to the listeners' version of the משנה, not רב's own.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's words 'הלכה כרבי מאיר' seemed to name the author according to רב's own reversed version, which would be a contradiction.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב used the name from his listeners' version. The law he follows, 'here is yours before you' for slaves, stays the same.
